Project Description:
Mahur or Mahurgad is a town and a pilgrim center of great religious significance as the three important temples of Renuka Mata, Dattatreya and Anasuya Mata are built on three mountain ranges. Each year on Dassehra, a fair is organized, and a lot of devotees visit Mahur on Datta Purnima. The different festivals celebrated during the year are of Gudi padwa, Nagpanchami, Shravan Shudh Trayodashi and Pola. Owing to the increasing devotees to these temples on hill tops and difficulties encountered climbing the steep steps, especially by older devotees and kids; it is proposed to upgrade the facilities by providing Lift, Skywalk and other amenities from the bottom of the hills to the temple tops.
Public Works Division (PWD), Bhokar, Nanded, Maharashtra is the implementing agency for the proposed project of Lift, Skywalk & other amenities. Project Description:
The proposed Pumped Storage Project consists of two schemes. The first scheme is proposed on the right bank with an installed capacity of 1200 MW, which comprises of an underground powerhouse housing 3 units of 300 MW and 2 units of 150 MW. The scheme envisages utilization of available head of upper reservoir and lower reservoir at an elevation of El.688.00 m (at FRL) and El. 166.00 m (at FRL) respectively. Both the reservoirs are interconnected through two individual water conductor systems, and the generator-motor and pump-turbines are installed at the underground powerhouse in between the reservoirs.
The second scheme is proposed on the left bank with an installed capacity of 3000MW. The proposed scheme comprises of an underground powerhouse accommodating 9 units of 300 MW and 2 units of 150 MW. The scheme is planned to utilize the available head between the upper reservoir and lower reservoir at an elevation of El. 678.00 m (at FRL) and El. 166.00 m (at FRL) respectively.

Project Description: There is no existing connectivity between Millat Nagar and Shahid Bhagat Singh Road, Goregaon Creek. Also, the proposed Coastal Road us passing by the Creek Road hence this bridge will be useful for dispersal of traffic from Millat Nagar to Bhagat Singh Nagar. Vehicles can use this alternate road instead of going from BEST colony road and then to Link Road. The alignment is as per the Development Plan of Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation. There is a provision of footpaths inclusive of utility corridor. The bridge is designed for all loads evaluated as per IRC6-2017. The proposed bridge cross creeklet and mangroves. In order to cause least damage to the mangrove a long span bridge has been preferred. Among the various choices of long span types, Cable stayed bridge was selected, keeping in mind the marine ecosystem, ease of construction, cost.

Project Description:
The proposal envisages by installing a PSP between two newly created reservoirs away from any major river course, by installing reversible Francis turbines of total installed capacity 1500 MW (5 x 250 MW for large unit and 2 x125 MW small unit).
This project is Open loop PSP where the reservoirs are not connected with any natural river sources. The Project comprises of upper & lower, out of which upper reservoir is to be constructed on the hill top with natural depression with max dam height of 73m to create the desired storage capacity while the lower reservoir will have maximum height of 72m constructed in a natural depression valley downhill. The scheme of operation for the project is with 6.32 Hours of peak power per day and 6.95 Hours for pumping back the water to the upper reservoir. Water will be used cyclically for energy storage and discharge. Evaporation losses, if any will be recouped periodically.

Project Description:
The proposal envisages by installing a PSP between two newly created reservoirs away from any major river course, by installing reversible Francis turbines of total installed capacity 1500 MW (5 x 250 MW for large unit and 2 x125 MW small unit).
This project is Open loop PSP where the reservoirs are not connected with any natural river sources. The Project comprises of upper & lower, out of which upper reservoir is to be constructed on the hill top with natural depression with max dam height of 73m to create the desired storage capacity while the lower reservoir will have maximum height of 72m constructed in a natural depression valley downhill. The scheme of operation for the project is with 6.32 Hours of peak power per day and 6.95 Hours for pumping back the water to the upper reservoir. Water will be used cyclically for energy storage and discharge. Evaporation losses, if any will be recouped periodically.

Project Description:
The Mandev Temple, nestled amidst the serene beauty of the forest, faces a critical challenge due to the proximity of a four-lane national highway that passes adjacent to the temple premises. The high intensity of traffic on this highway, combined with sharp turns in the road, poses a serious risk of road accidents in the vicinity of the temple area.  During their visits, devotees prepare food as Prasad / naivedyam for Lord Shiva in the open forest area, utilizing firewood collected from the forest itself. Regrettably, the use of plastic plates and pet glasses for serving food has led to the indiscriminate disposal of waste in the forest area after use, contributing to environmental degradation and defacement of the natural surroundings.
By providing devotees with a designated Devotee Utility Center and Parking Area, we aim to enhance the overall experience of visitors to the Mandev Temple while also safeguarding the natural beauty of the surrounding forest area.

Project Description:
The Mandev Temple, nestled amidst the serene beauty of the forest, faces a critical challenge due to the proximity of a four-lane national highway that passes adjacent to the temple premises. The high intensity of traffic on this highway, combined with sharp turns in the road, poses a serious risk of road accidents in the vicinity of the temple area.  During their visits, devotees prepare food as Prasad / naivedyam for Lord Shiva in the open forest area, utilizing firewood collected from the forest itself. Regrettably, the use of plastic plates and pet glasses for serving food has led to the indiscriminate disposal of waste in the forest area after use, contributing to environmental degradation and defacement of the natural surroundings.

This proposal benefits both the tribal population, wildlife, and the BMC.

Project Description: The plot bearing survey No 340 is located near Vasai creek and been used for salt production prior to 1836. Said plot is demarcated as CRZ I A (Mangrove), CRZ I A(Mangrove buffer zone), CRZ I B (Intertidal Zone) and CRZ II as per approved CZMP 2019. As per CRZ notification amendments   dated 1st May 2020 , in case there exists a bund or a sluice gate constructed in the past, prior to the date of notification issued vide S.0. 114(E) dated 19th February 1991, the HTL shall be restricted up to the line long along the bund or the sluice gate”. Therefore as the  existence of the saltpan dates back to 1836, the presence of bund around salt pan is referred as High Tide Line. Therefore the plot under reference lying beyond HTL and  demarcated as CRZ I(B) need to be revised as non CRZ in the CZMP 2019 as per provision made for revision in CZMP as per CRZ notification 2019.

It is a small mine and transportation and haulage of stone will be carried out by tractors/ trucks within quarry and onward dispatch to various customers will be by tippers. There is no human settlement in the lease area. No ground water will be encountered in the pit. There is no historical monuments of structures of any importance in core zone or in the buffer zone. The rock is hard , compact massive rock and there is no erosion. No wet processing is adopted. proposed workings area is of shallow depth and mostly carried out in dry seasons. Drains will be made at key places to guide rain water so that erosion is avoided. The mining operation will be of manual nature and loading will be manual.

Project Description: The proposed bridge intends to connect two talukas viz. Bhiwandi & Thane. The proposed road will start from Ghodbunder Road at Kasarvadavali and ends to Major State Highway 4 (Chinchoti-Anjur Phata Road) at Kharbav. Currently both the corridors are not connected anywhere in-between the Ahmedabad Highway and Nashik Highway. It is vital road segment of Radial-2 (Part of NH-3) as Regional Corridor proposed in Regional Plan and Updating for Comprehensive Transport Study of MMRDA. The link will connect Thane with regional corridors including Virar-Alibaug multimodal corridor and also provide easy access for vehicles travelling between JNPT, Navi Mumbai, Mumbai, Thane and Bhiwandi that will not have to make a detour via Ghodbunder. This  nalla originate on a Minor ridge in Kalasgade Village and Dhamane village area flows from North to South & joins to Tillari River on Right bank. The proposed project area, characterized by large valleys and mountains, receives consistent and substantial rainfall, ensuring the availability of significant water storage in Paleparmar nala. This water resource can be effectively utilized for additional power generation. It is proposed to divert water from the Paleparmar Nala to the existing power canal of the Tilari Hydro Electric Project Stage - I, thereby significantly increasing hydroelectric power generation at the site.

The project will provide clean drinking water to the Pabal Plateau settlement and schools, support irrigation for agriculture, supply water for livestock, and create small waterholes for wildlife conservation. Project Description:
The proposed Savitri Pumped Storage Project (2400MW), a self-identified off stream open loop project, is being developed by the NHPC around two
adjacent valleys drained by the Koyna River and Savitri River in District Satara, and Raigad, Maharashtra. The upper and lower dams for the PSP are proposed to be newly constructed. The proposed upper dam (embankment/GFRD) is located across Koyna River, which is a tributary of Krishna River, in Jaoli village near Mahabaleshwar, Satara district. The proposed lower dam (concrete gravity) is located across Savitri River near Lahulase village, Tehsil Poladpur, Raigad district. The water for initial filling of both reservoirs/ recoupment of evaporation and re-circulation losses shall be met from rainfall yield of self-catchment of the lower reservoir only. The water conductor system, surge shafts, powerhouse and TRT shall be totally underground. The tentative cost of project is Rs 11826 Crores.
EC Consultant: EQMS Global Pvt. Ltd. formerly known as EQMS India Pvt. Ltd.
Project Name: Savitri Pumped Storage Project (2400 MW)

Project Description:
the Ajanta Caves Rail Connectivity between Jalna and Jalgaon covers a proposed 174 km Broad Gauge (BG) line under the Central Railway. The project aims to provide a direct, efficient, and sustainable transportation corridor connecting Marathwada and Khandesh regions of Maharashtra. The alignment passes through the districts of Jalna, Aurangabad, and Jalgaon, enhancing connectivity to the UNESCO World Heritage Ajanta Caves and supporting socio-economic growth in the region.
The new railway line will reduce the travel distance between Jalna and Jalgaon from approximately 336 km to 174 km, decreasing travel time from over 5 hours to about 3.5 hours. This project intends to stimulate tourism, industrial activity, agriculture, and logistics in rural Maharashtra, while ensuring improved connectivity from Gujarat to Andhra Pradesh and Southern India.

Project Description:
The project involves construction of a groyne-type bund and maintenance and clearing of a navigational channel at Waravade Creek, Ratnagiri, Maharashtra. Clearing and maintenance of navigational channel will involve dredging of Waravade creek up to –2 m chart datum over the harbour entrance to maintain draft. The total area to be dredged is 38,097.73 sq.m. The dredged sand will be relocated to the nearby Undi beach for shoreline stabilization. 
The plan calls for a 564 m-long rubble-mound training wall laid out parallel to Waravade creek and the fishing channel entrance, with a graded stone cross-section—bedding, core, underlayer, heavy armour sized for a 6.08 m (100-year) design wave, and toe protection—designed per SPM and IS 4651 guidelines. By intercepting littoral drift, maintaining a –2 m draft in the harbour entrance, and promoting sediment build-up behind the wall, it ensures year-round tranquility and supplies material for adjacent beach nourishment.

Project Description:
Geological mapping on a 1:12,500 scale was conducted in and around the Plasgaon and Wadhona areas, covering 100 sq. km, in part of the Survey of India Toposheet No. 55P/11 in Chandrapur District, Maharashtra. During the course of mapping, a promising copper occurrence was identified in the Wadhona–Awalgaon/Umargaon area, which requires confirmation through exploratory drilling.
Considering copper’s significance as a critical mineral and its vital role in green energy technologies, exploratory drilling has been planned to establish sub-surface continuity and to assess the resource potential of copper and associated mineralization. The proposed investigation block covers an area of approximately 2.0 sq. km, within which a total of seven (07) boreholes are planned for drilling.
Of these, one (01) borehole—of 56 mm (2.20 inch) diameter—is located within the Protected Forest area of Alewahi Beat/Round in the Talodhi Range, Brahmapuri Forest Division, Chandrapur Circle

The proposed project involves development of an All-Weather, Greenfield, Multi-cargo, Deepwater Port at Murbe, Palghar Dist, Maharashtra by JSW Infrastructure Limited. The proposed port is envisaged to handle captive cargo of JSW group and also handle opportunity cargo from hinterland industries. The proposed port will serve the needs of the hinterland comprising of Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation Area (MIDC), Tarapur Industrial Area (TIA), Vapi & Valsad Industrial Area (VIA) and other industrial & business hubs in the proximity.
The port shall be designed to handle about 134.07 MTPA various solid and liquid cargos, viz. Bulk, Break Bulk, Container, Automobile, Project cargo and Liquid Cargos, etc. The proposed cargo will be handled in 16 berths (2 bulk berths, 2 multipurpose berths, 9 container berths, 3 liquid cargo berths, and 2 berth for port crafts/tugs). Port will be protected by 2 breakwaters (10 km south breakwater and 1.3 km offshore north breakwater).

Project Description: The Dangurli High Level Barrage project is proposed on the Wainganga River in the Godavari Basin near Dangurli village in Gondia taluka, Gondia district. The proposed barrage will have a length of 450 meters with a live storage capacity of 10.91 million cubic meters. The stored water will strengthen the existing three lift irrigation schemes located upstream of the Dangurli barrage i.e. Tedhwa-Shivani L.I.S., Dangurli L.I.S., and Navegaon-Deori L.I.S. by providing irrigation facilities to a cumulative Culturable Command Area (CCA) of 8635.25 ha in Gondia taluka. In addition to irrigation benefits, the proposed storage will ensure assured water availability for domestic purposes, including drinking water supply to Gondia city. Further, the creation of a reservoir will provide opportunities for fisheries development, generating additional livelihood avenues and contributing to the socio-economic upliftment of the local population.

Both reservoirs are situated on non-perennial nallahs with negligible natural inflow. The project envisages construction of upper dam (GRFD; Length:536.65m; Height: 41.22m) and lower dam (Concrete; Length:550.19m; Height:56.65m). The water conductor system and powerhouse (4x300MW) shall be totally underground.  The annual energy generation in turbine mode for daily 6.14 hours shall be 2556.37 MU whereas annual energy consumption in pump mode for 7.20 hours is 3295.59 MU.
EC Consultant: EQMS Global Pvt. Ltd. formerly known as EQMS India Pvt. Ltd.

Project Description: The Bodwad Parisar Sinchan Yojana is a major irrigation project under the Tapi Irrigation Development Corporation aimed at improving water availability in the Tapi River Basin of Jalgaon District. The project proposes lifting 198.54 Mcum of water from the Purna River near Khamkheda Bridge close to Muktainagar, which will be stored in the Junone and Jamthi reservoirs. It will be implemented in two phases: Phase I includes construction of the Junone Storage Reservoir (120.78 Mcum) with water lifted in two stages, while Phase II involves construction of the Jamthi Storage Reservoir (42.91 Mcum) supplied from the Junone Dam distribution tank. The project plans a total water utilisation of 197.574 Mcum and is expected to provide irrigation benefits to 101 villages across Jalgaon District and Buldhana District, particularly in the talukas of Jamner, Muktainagar, Bodwad, Motala, and Malkapur, with the goal of improving agricultural productivity and ensuring reliable irrigation in the region.

Project Description: The proposed Humbarli Birmani Pumped Storage Project is an open- loop system located in Satara and Ratnagiri Districts, Maharashtra. Both reservoirs are situated on non-perennial nallahs with negligible natural inflow. The project envisages the construction of an upper dam (GFRD; Length:607.66m; Height:51.09m) and a lower dam (Concrete; Length:567.04m; Height:76.15m). The water conductor system and powerhouse (6x250MW) shall be totally underground.  The annual energy generation in turbine mode for a daily 6.17 hours shall be 3207.44 MU, whereas the annual energy consumption in pump mode for 7.17 hours is 4104.50 MU.

Project Description:
Ahupe, Balvirwadi, and Kondhwal are villages situated within the tribal regions of Ambegaon Tehsil, an area characterized by hilly terrain and high annual rainfall. The road proposed for improvement is designated as Major District Road (MDR-165). Currently, this route remains an unpaved (kachcha) track, necessitating an upgrade to ensure year-round connectivity.
The road proposed for improvement is the primary link connecting these villages. Due to heavy rainfall, the road has sustained significant damage and requires immediate restoration to ensure a safe daily commute. The Government has issued AA & TS to improve the proposed  unpaved road bituminous surface. The extant road proposed for improvement traverse through certain patches of Reserved Forest Land falling within the limits of the Bhimashankar Wildlife Sanctuary.  As such, the project attracts provisions of VSSA, 1980 & W(P)A, 1972.

Project Description:
Sangamner is a historic city in Maharashtra. It has an area of approximately 6.3 square kilometers and is densely populated. The city's population exceeds one lakh. Due to increasing urbanization, industrial establishments, educational institutions, hospitals, and commercial complexes, the city has experienced rapid growth. Consequently, the movement of people and vehicles has increased significantly, leading to changes in the local environment.
In recent years, the number of stray animals, particularly stray dogs, has increased considerably in Sangamner city. Due to the lack of an adequate Animal Birth Control (ABC) facility, the stray dog population continues to grow. Project Description: The proposed exploration scheme for the Naokari Budruk Limestone Block (1.25 sq. km) in Rajura Taluka, Chandrapur District, aims to establish G-3 level limestone resources in accordance with MEMC Rules, 2015. Project Description: The proposed 240 MW Tilari Pumped Storage Project (PSP) is an off-stream, closed-loop pumped storage scheme located near Kodali Village in Chandgad Taluka, Maharashtra. The project will utilize the existing Kodali Forebay Reservoir as the upper reservoir, which has a gross storage capacity of 2.145 MCM and an FRL of 727.23 m. A new lower reservoir with a live storage capacity of 2.533 MCM is proposed in a natural depression near Kodali Village. The project will operate by pumping water from the lower reservoir to the upper reservoir during off-peak hours and releasing it through reversible pump-turbines to generate electricity during peak demand. This arrangement enhances grid reliability, supports renewable energy integration, and provides efficient energy storage without significant dependence on river inflows, as the project operates in a closed-loop system with minimal environmental impact.

Project Description: Proposed 5400 MW Pumped Storage Project is Off-Stream Open Loop pumped storage hydroelectric project. The Project comprises of upper & lower reservoirs with a gross storage capacity of 27.97 MCM & 27.38 MCM respectively. The upper reservoir is proposed to be constructed on the hill top with maximum dam height of 78.00 m (from deepest bed level) to create the desired storage capacity. The lower reservoir will have maximum height of 77.00 m (from deepest bed level) proposed to be constructed at the downhill. The scheme for operation for the project is 6.58 hours of peak hour generation per day and 7.77 hours for pumping back the water to the upper reservoir. Being an off-stream open loop project, 36.50 MCM of water will be required for one time filling of the reservoir which will be carried out from the self-catchment inflows of the Lower Reservoir, evaporation losses (2.50 MCM) will be recouped periodically from the catchment itself.

Project Description:
The project starts from AEML Tower no SS 321 at Marve village having an underground cable network for a length of 4.0 km ending at 220kV EHV Sub-Station in Kandivali in Mumbai taluka. The Duct bank construction in the Project involves trench excavation followed by bed PCC then laying of HDPE Pipes with proper alignment and spacing. The ducts are encased in concrete for mechanical protection, after which Tiles & warning tape is placed and backfield with soil. Tower construction includes foundation excavation and casting as per design, followed by erection of the monopole/tower using cranes. Stringing/tapping of the conductor is then completed to connect with the underground cable system.
The project ensures a reliable and uninterrupted power supply to the Kandivali–Malad region by strengthening the transmission network and improving overall stability.

Project Description:
Kalyan-Asangaon Railway line from Ch. 53.404 to Km. Ch. 85.64 (32.23 Km) is electrified double line section of Mumbai Division and its augmentation to 3rd line is under progress. This corridor is known as the North-East Main Lines and is a part of CSTM-HWH Group ‘A’ route. It 
is divided into two sub-sections viz. Kalyan-Titwala (10.84 km) works on Automatic Block Signaling and Titwala-Asangaon (21.38 Km) on Absolute Block System. All the three streams of traffic viz. Suburban, Mail / Express and freight trains use the same pair of lines between Kalyan & Asangaon. Beyond Titwala, the section has a highly undulating terrain with ruling gradient of 1 in 90 in DN direction and 1 in 132 in UP direction. 
Central Railway (CR), Mumbai Division is the implementing agency for the proposed 4th railway line between Kalyan and Asangaon stations.
